=== DOCS-TRUTH (verified 2026-06-08 via WebFetch) ===

• [trino.io/docs/467/connector/iceberg.html](https://trino.io/docs/467/connector/iceberg.html) — Iceberg ALTER TABLE EXECUTE optimize: file_size_threshold parameter is a DataSize-typed value requiring a unit suffix. Docs example verbatim: `ALTER TABLE test_table EXECUTE optimize(file_size_threshold => '128MB')`. Default value: `100MB`. The doc string and example both confirm a quoted size literal with a recognized unit; the docs do NOT show a bare-bytes form anywhere.
• 134217728 bytes = 128 * 1024 * 1024 = 128MB (binary MB / mebibyte) — confirmed by arithmetic and consistent with the Iceberg default `write.target-file-size-bytes` of 536870912 (= 512MB). 268435456 = 256MB. 1073741824 = 1GB.
• [trino.io/docs/467/sql/select.html](https://trino.io/docs/467/sql/select.html) — window frame default: 'If the frame is not specified, it defaults to RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING, which is the same as RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW. This frame contains all rows from the start of the partition up to the last peer of the current row.' Confirms (a) default is RANGE; (b) RANGE includes peers (lumps tied ORDER BY values); (c) by complement, ROWS is positional and each physical row gets its own frame.
• [trino.io/blog/2021/03/10/introducing-new-window-features.html](https://trino.io/blog/2021/03/10/introducing-new-window-features.html) — supporting quote: 'When using CURRENT ROW in a RANGE frame, it includes all rows where values of the sort key are the same as in the current row, which are called a peer group.' Confirms the iter587 card's RANGE-peer-group fact.
